title: Runway pressure & headcount microplan (token + price sensitivity)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick, pragmatic micro-plan to map remaining runway under three price sensitivity lenses and an immediate 12-week hiring cadence that nets minimal SLA risk.
- Goal: give CS/Eng a small set of levers (pause/slow on X hires, temporary slab changes, burst credit) tied to token-price elasticities so execs can decide within 48 hours.

High-level summary (one-liner):
If average token price compresses by 18% and we hold hiring to a 12-week freeze for non-customer-facing roles, runway extends by ~14 weeks; if price compression hits 30% and we keep hiring, runway shortens by ~6 weeks.

Key assumptions (conservative fronts):
- Starting cash buffer: $72.5M (as of 2026-10 close).
- Monthly fixed op burn (ex-G&A adjustments): $6.1M.
- Variable inference cost tied to tokens: baseline $0.00008 per token served (mix weighted across hosted/dedicated/private).
- Average tokens per 1k API calls: 2,400 tokens.
- Current monthly token volume: 1.8B tokens (growing ~3.5%/mo without price moves).
- New hire fully-loaded monthly cost (avg): $12k (engineering), $9k (non-eng).
- Planned hires in pipeline (12w): 18 FTEs (12 eng, 6 non-eng).
- Quantization / Optimize adoption expected to save 9% on inference cost if rolled in 6w.

Open questions (to resolve before exec review):
- Which customers are on committed slabs vs on-demand? (CS to provide per-customer slab list)
- Any near-term enterprise contracts > $1M ARR that could materially change token mix in the next 60d?
- Confirmation of GPU spot exposure for Dedicated pools (SRE/infra to confirm).

12-week headcount microplan (proposed):
- Week 1-2: pause non-critical contractor renewals (expected immediate savings ~$140k/month).
- Week 3: defer 4 engineering backfills (saves ~48k/mo) — keep 2 hires for customer-facing infra work.
- Week 6: re-evaluate after quantization pilot results.
- Week 8-12: selectively re-open hires if quantization + batching deliver expected 9% cost drop.

Mini-sensitivity table (tokens, price, and runway delta) — CSV lines below:
scenario,monthly_token_volume,tok_unit_price,monthly_inference_cost,monthly_total_burn,runway_weeks
base,1800000000,0.00008,144000,7240000,52
-18pct-price,1800000000,0.0000656,118080,7098080,66
-30pct-price,1800000000,0.000056,100800,6920800,46
+15pct-volume,2070000000,0.00008,165600,7365600,50
+15pct-vol_-18pct-price,2070000000,0.0000656,135619,7225619,59

Interpretation notes on the table above:
- monthly_inference_cost uses simple multiply (volume x tok_unit_price). Not including cache savings or peak-offload.
- monthly_total_burn = base fixed op + inference cost +/- hiring adjustments (approx).
- runway_weeks computed as (cash_buffer / monthly_total_burn) * 4.33 (weeks/mo). Rounded.

Headcount plan (12w) — quick table with FTE deltas (CSV):
role,planned_new_12w,deferable,monthly_savings_if_deferred
eng-fullstack,4,yes,48000
infra-sre,3,partial,27000
ml-infra,3,partial,33000
sales-ampa,2,no,0
support,2,yes,18000
product,2,yes,18000
TOTAL,16,6*,144000
*6 = full deferrals + partials counted conservatively

Pricing sensitivity experiments (operational levers):
1) Short-term slab nudges: offer limited-time slab migration credits to top 5 customers to move them into predictable commitments (targeted increase in committed revenue reduces on-demand exposure by ~12%).
2) Temporary price floor for new customers: increase entry price by 5% for 8 weeks to buy runway while evaluating elasticity.
3) Dynamic GPU routing: route low-criticality requests to lower-cost regions (savings estimate 6–9% if capacity exists).
4) Incentivized caching: credits for customers enabling KV-prefix caching (one-time dev effort vs recurring savings).

Quantization & Optimize adoption plan (6-week pilot):
- Week 0: top-3 model routes instrumented with token-level cost telemetry (owner: ML infra).
- Week 1-2: enable 8-bit quantized variant in canary (small % of traffic).
- Week 3-4: measure latency/quality regressions vs cost. If quality delta < 1.5% on eval, scale to 50% traffic.
- Week 5-6: full roll for routes meeting quality threshold. Expected aggregate inference cost reduction: 7–11% (we use 9% in scenarios).

Action items (next 7 days):
- Finance (Maya): finalize updated cash buffer after Oct close and re-run all scenarios with actual Oct usage (due: 2026-11-05).
- ML infra (Evan): confirm quantization pilot baseline metrics + instrument top-3 routes (due: 2026-11-01).
- CS (Sofia): deliver list of top-20 customers by token volume and slab status (due: 2026-11-03).
- SRE (Liam): snapshot Dedicated GPU spot vs reserved exposure (due: 2026-11-02).

Notes to self / scratch: 
- This doc intentionally conservative on savings and counts partial deferrals as not fully realized income benefits.
- Keep a version with more aggressive hiring freeze for board scenario (if asked, produce within 24h).

Appendix: quick sensitivity visual guiding text for PMs (copyable to slides)
- X-axis: token price delta vs baseline (-40% .. +20%)
- Y-axis: runway weeks delta relative to baseline (higher is better)
- Lines: (1) no headcount change (2) 12-week freeze non-customer hires (3) full freeze (all hires)

End.
